translations.answer: The project maintainer explicitly states that the current GPU does not support the surface-velocity behavior, and it should be used with CPU. The original post verified that regular colliders still contact the surface by testing both the new PhysxSurfaceVelocityAPI and the legacy velocity attribute in the ConveyorBeltDemo. The triggering condition is the GPU tensor pipeline with surface velocity enabled. If it must remain on GPU, the original post only records an approximate scheme for gradually rewriting the horizontal root velocity of static colliders; it is not equivalent to the native contact and cannot be used to validate friction or contact force.
translations.applicability: Directly covers Isaac Sim 5.0/PhysX 107.3.26 GPU tensor pipeline; Isaac Lab precise commit not filled, subsequent versions need retesting.
translations.credibility.rationale: Environmental, processing steps, and results have engineering records, but formal cross-verification or independent replication is missing.
translations.details.attempts.0: The original post tested both the new PhysxSurfaceVelocityAPI and the legacy velocity attribute in the ConveyorBeltDemo under the same GPU tensor pipeline, and they showed identical behavior.
translations.details.attempts.1: The regular contact is restored after disabling surface velocity.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: The same scene was tested with CPU and GPU, with four grid comparisons, and only surfaceVelocityEnabled was switched to isolate the collider and surface velocity function.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: The object's z-coordinate, horizontal velocity, and whether it fell to the ground were recorded to avoid relying solely on the viewport.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: When a native surface velocity contact is required, the CPU pipeline should be used.
translations.details.effective_fixes.1: The original post's GPU workaround is an approximate scheme for static colliders, which is not equivalent to the native contact and cannot be used to validate friction or contact force.
translations.details.environments.0: Isaac Sim 5.0; omni.physx 107.3.26; Ubuntu 22.04.5; RTX 4090; CUDA 13.0; driver 580.173.02; device=cpu/cuda:0 comparison.
translations.details.limits.0: The Isaac Lab commit/version field in the System Info is not filled, only confirming Isaac Sim/PhysX, OS, GPU, CUDA, and driver.
translations.details.limits.1: Writing the root velocity directly bypasses real friction and impulse response, and cannot be used to validate contact force or control stability.
translations.details.limits.2: No information provided about the GPU support recovery version or patch.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The maintainer states that the behavior is within the current supported boundary and requires CPU; Issue is closed with 'completed', but the native GPU surface velocity is not implemented.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: After enabling PhysX surface velocity in the Isaac Lab GPU tensor pipeline, the object passes through the conveyor belt; is this due to a collider or friction configuration error?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Do not use the GPU contact tunneling phenomenon for parameter tuning or training contact strategies; first verify the contact function boundary by switching to CPU, and separate the approximate behavior from physical contact experiments.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: The project maintainer confirms that the current GPU does not support this surface-velocity behavior; it is not a failure of the collider itself.
translations.details.symptoms.0: The CPU tensor pipeline causes the block to stop at z ≈ 0.30 and move at the conveyor belt speed; the GPU tensor pipeline causes the block to pass through the conveyor belt and land at z ≈ 0.0375 with zero horizontal velocity.
translations.details.symptoms.1: No warning/error; the regular GPU contact is restored simply by disabling surfaceVelocityEnabled.
translations.source.locator: Isaac Lab #6885: four-configuration comparison and minimal script in the main report; maintainer comment 5196164192 confirms that GPU is unsupported and requires CPU
translations.source.title: The Isaac Lab GPU tensor pipeline does not currently support PhysX surface-velocity contact
translations.title: What is the current supported boundary and handling method for the same kinematic conveyor belt in CPU normal and GPU tensor pipeline with PhysX surface velocity enabled?
